steps.analyst_reply: {"root_cause": "The scorecard relies on a single holistic surgeon-vs-physician judgment, and it fails in two recurring ways. First, most errors are surgeons whose texts contain explicit surgical signals (\"specialize in Surgery\", \"board certified in Plastic/Orthopaedic Surgery\", valve replacement, facial reconstruction, operating-room neurosurgery) that the holistic answer overlooks amid insurance and rating boilerplate. Second, several false 'surgeon' calls are mid-level practitioners (\"Mr./Ms. X practices medicine and specializes in Orthopaedic Surgery\") whom the labeled data consistently marks as physician regardless of specialty, a distinction the holistic question never isolates.", "add_elements": [{"key": "mentions_surgical_practice", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text state that this person performs surgery, works in the operating room, or specializes in, is board certified in, or practices a surgical field such as general, orthopaedic, plastic, neuro, cardiac, vascular, hand, or dental surgery, or list surgical procedures such as joint or valve replacement, tumor removal, or facial reconstruction among their services?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "midlevel_clinician", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this person referred to as Mr. or Ms. rather than Dr., or identified as a physician assistant or nurse practitioner rather than as a medical doctor?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "nonsurgical_medical_practice", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text indicate this person practices a non-surgical medical field such as family or internal medicine, general practice, endocrinology, gastroenterology, dermatology, or emergency medicine, or list non-surgical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, warts, or infections among their clinical interests?", "criteria": null}], "retire_elements": [], "reword_elements": []}
